notes.title: Announcing Release Date
notes.notes:
Alone is finally close to release, having been in early access for three years, and a number of milestones later, the game is finally now stable, and featured enough to release it properly.

This release also includes some new features - the "Rune" milestone, which includes graphical improvements, the addition of embeddable runes, changes to trade, and much more.

The release also sees Alone getting a small tweak to its name.

If you're just here for the release date - then here it is :) - October 11th

If you're interested in everything else coming out in this milestone, then read on...


Name Change
With the upcoming release - the game will be known as Alone: Shattered Tribes.

There are multiple reasons for this change. Firstly, when this name was bequeathed, it was a very very different game - there were no tribes to save, it was an unforgiving survival RPG, and you would actually spend the entire game alone. With the updates made to the game since then, this is no longer the case, and the name is no longer accurate.

This new name reflects the game itself - where you start off alone, but you must unite the shattered tribes in your new home.

You might also notice some changes in the steam page, with a new fancy logo and other similar changes


New Trailer
With a new release comes a new trailer, and here it is :)


[previewyoutube="cHdzJrj-RXs;full"][/previewyoutube]

Graphic Changes
One of the main changes coming with this release is an update to the way the terrain and lighting look. The sharp square tiles are gone, and replaced with something more beautiful looking.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/9a06b0f8d0c7aa87c8fc39a64faa0cd8b21d7f85.png"]

The lighting has also been adjusted, there's more visibility during night-time, and when exploring dark areas.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/47dac484d2f59ba1b612e0db8a088c75d6c89b00.png"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ec25c70c37b08938440c468148cc24ba0105a63d.png"]
Runes & Elixirs
The namesake of the update is the Rune system. Runes are rare items which are embedded into weapons to give them great power.

Runes can be found randomly as loot, but they can be more reliably obtained by exploring the Crypt.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/96cc6108915cdbb07894e8446f960f04f3fcc882.png"]

Certain Crypt levels will contain a room like the one shown above. After defeating the enemies guarding it, you can claim one of 7 different types of runes.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/30ed4fdb8ac41f4693a22d5e627197685eec369b.png"]

Runes are then embedded into weapons at the shrine. 

Some runes will give a flat bonus of some sort, such as finding nicer loot or gaining faster experience, but other runes need to be charged.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1682e27ce11a4e4c70ea880146b14a0a4e33e0c2.png"]

Charging a rune involves defeating enemies, after which you can invoke the power of the rune - a powerful, yet very temporary bonus. Continuing to defeat enemies whilst the rune is active will help recharge it, giving you more time to make use of its powers. Some of the more powerful runes will only trigger when enemies of certain types are defeated.



Runes come in three levels, with the Mythical runes being the most rare. However, one can Empower runes at the shrine to gain access to more powerful ones, at the sacrifice of 2 other runes which are destroyed in the process.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f280eac2d2252a66d624760094da76558a68e7d2.png"]



The intention of this new feature is to allow the player to customise weapons for specific uses. With the more powerful runes restricted to impacting only specific enemy types, having a weapon for each scenario will be the key to maximising benefits.


Elixirs
This update also brings with it changes to Elixirs. They are much rarer and more precious now.

Additionally, the elixir of healing has been split into three levels:

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8f85c4c8517c9fc33369a5bfc7f8e4b6e89bfb6e.png"]

Each level will, when drunk, restore your health by a limited amount. At lower levels, the Minor Elixir should be enough, but as you increase in levels, it will no longer heal you fully, and you'll need to make use of the more expensive, and rarer elixirs.


Trader Improvements
Trading has been reworked extensively.

Previously, trade had some limitations which made it less useful, and quite lacking. Traders were specialised, bringing two classes of items with each visit - for instance, a trader bringing only weapons and armour.

This is quite limiting, as not all items are equally desirable. Coupled with the limitation added on the quality of items that are generated, meant that traders which brought weapons or tools would often be ignored, with raw goods traders being far more useful.

Moreover, the traders focused primarily on quantity instead of quality. So it would be more likely that a trader brings a large number of cheaper items, instead of a few expensive ones.

This milestone changes everything. Now each trader has a certain, fixed, amount of slots. Each slot is restricted to the type of item which it can bring - although some slots are general. This way, the trader is guaranteed to always bring some raw materials and some food with each visit. As the trader becomes richer, they will still bring the same amount of slots, but each item will cost more - meaning higher quality weapons, tools, and armour, and more useful raw materials.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1e8fc7e15a91f5343c582fb61805f9b90ee41231.png"]

Additionally, the first slot is guaranteed to be an exotic good. These are goods which can only be obtained through trade - such as fertiliser, or silk. These existed previously, primarily as some late-game building upgrades - but because of the way the items were generated previously, did not show up as often as desired.

As part of this milestone, quite a few exotic items have been added - there is now more exotic food, the inclusion of exotic beverages, as well as weapons and armour.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/763492a3cdf4ebe482296a1272eafb382b4632d4.png"]

Here's a character kitted out with one of the choices of exotic helmet, armour and weapon.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e7a6f463c7192f919cb6a36a8b294d1e47526621.png"]

If slots are fixed, then how does one go about getting more items? Through trade upgrades

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/77a49ac1991774f6620210df5b9e1684e33da57f.png"]

Whilst expensive, you can add up to two additional slots.

And these slots are customisable - so you can choose what exactly the trader will bring 

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/87f4ad1bc9ab072009ce3ce8f0eb3bd7cafcfc91.png"]

This can be changed freely whenever a trader is visiting, and will impact any upcoming traders. By planning ahead, you can ensure you will find the specific items you're looking to buy.



With these changes, the trader should become much more useful, and also grant access to powerful and rare items for those with deep pockets


Everpunished
The Everpunished have received some changes as well.

Firstly, they now look different, the basic melee Everpunished appearing in three variants making it more clear how dangerous they are. Also they look nicer, just thought I'd mention that.



[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/a8f28fb783646c4f343c33cc9048cb267ef5193d.png"]

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c470c5482051acec33385619b9baed64544ce4a1.png"]

In a manner similar to how goblin armies are equipped, as you descend to deeper levels, there are new enemy types which replace the easier ones. For the Everpunished, this includes the crossbow draugr, which replaces the axe thrower.

 [img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/931327b0b0223956573b50262c60ac38331ed88e.png"]

And similar to their goblin counterparts, they will on occasion grant you a temporary penalty if they succeed on a critical hit.

They are further joined by the banshee, who's screams strike terror into your heart

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/6f0859ebe3d55eb958dc899220ec222ac4eb8d5d.png"]


Forest
The forest has also seen some improvement.

Whilst it will remain a place for early, lower level, hunts - if you traverse far enough, you will find something more dangerous.

This is one of three types of "boss" enemies.

[img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/87d089a0cbf5d578dd62f129a462c94a2842a458.png"]

Each of them have their own special attacks, and are formidable enemies in their own right. But defeating them will grant you some unique rewards, so it's worth the risk if you're strong enough.
Wrapping Up
And that's it :) See you on the 11th of October.

notes.title: Tribe Update Releasing Soon
notes.notes:
The Tribe Update drastically changes the late to end game. It replaces the blighted island concept and replaces it with a number of missions.

And it will be released soon - specifically on the 7th of December

Let's take a look at what to expect with this next release

New Trailer
With the large changes that this release will bring, it is only fitting that the trailer changes to reflect it.

[previewyoutube=nFlNPS5TGZ4;full][/previewyoutube]

The Story
This release introduces and fleshes out our hero's story. Their village having been razed by goblins and their companions taken captive, they escape, only to shipwreck on the island.

Our hero's story is now shown in a number of cutscenes which play before gameplay starts.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5864e8453efbd2677a2feab45900b4b22de46dd.png

And after having survived and settled on the island, our hero will work to unite the other tribes being menaced by the goblin foe, and hoping to finally rescue their companions.

A scene from their escape is also displayed in the main menu, and used for character customisation

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e0fc6fa3b45aee956adb035044c5c71dcb3def0b.png

Missions
The blighted lands concept has been changed and replaced by a number of missions.

After our hero repairs the ship, they can visit each island in turn, with each island containing a different mission.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/da81e70e299702aeaf5fa29f032228b6003ddf9f.png

With each mission, our hero finds a tribe which is in trouble, or takes the fight to the goblins. Each mission is entirely different, and whilst some of them do have procedurally generated maps, the rest have custom made maps and custom code to support them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/51f719e266ef7dff108122b2a5c4f35210e7e0f5.png

Most of the missions include some degree of combat, but with certain missions, the more economic focused hero can use their resources to make things easier.

For instance - this mission involves defending a fortress from waves of goblin attackers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/e3878f135a7cffb22584db38c9545c54bc43dec6.png

If we want to make the fight easier - we can purchase some mission specific upgrades - such as the healing supplies upgrade which allows you more healing.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/57af0971de9bd7a91b6b0e1189d655847e798624.png

This should allow players who prefer to focus on the economic side of the game, to made combat just that bit easier.

Blood Brothers
In previous versions of the game, blighted islands could be claimed and specific buildings could be placed to grant our hero some extra resources. This feature has been replaced by the concept of a Blood Brother. When completing each mission, the player will unlock at least one blood brother (some missions grant more than one).

By using the desk, the player can assign blood brothers to specific tasks.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/dab5f9f8980970a5465162e4592c2b3e8cbb1833.png

Depending on the task assigned, every day, our hero may find additional resources in their stockpile. Alternatively they can be assigned to a crafting building to give a bonus to the quality of the items produced. A third option is to assign a blood brother as a companion - this character will join you in the dangerous areas, and fight off enemies with their bow.

Tribehome & Services
A representation of the tribes that our hero is uniting can be found in the Tribehome. This location can be visited from the main island, and gradually expands as our hero completes more missions. With each expansion, the amount of villagers wandering increases, and so do the buildings.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5f8016becb909f45d1e1dc3c4a422879b3f61ca.png

Aside from being an interesting location to visit and watch grow, the tribehome also introduces a number of services. Some of the services are limited by the size of the tribehome.

One of the services on offer is the ability to repair one's weapons and tools. If our hero happens to be flush with a lot of money, they can also make use of the combat training on offer at the barracks - although this is expensive.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/7a235e54815c15cca6c91252a6da582dc4eeaf74.png

New Enemies
A new major update wouldn't be the same without some new enemies to fight. Aside from some special boss enemies, the goblins have also received some reinforcements, some of which have special abilities to make them more effective.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c8dcb1976cca0f111a66249fdf5cc4fa75ca30f8.png
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/a2aa589837874a6a36f80805a80821f24e0d30da.png

The rogue and the alchemist are just two of them. The rogue is able to land critical hits - and in so doing, applies a debuff which makes it easier for their friends to harm you.

The alchemist is able to occasionally throw bottles of toxic gas, which will make you weaker if you breathe in too much of them.

Wrapping it Up
There are many other smaller changes which I haven't mentioned here. I hope these changes will make the late to end game more fun.

notes.title: Alone | Domus Update Released
notes.notes:
It is my pleasure to announce the release of the next major update for Alone - Domus.

The focus of this update is the peaceful part of the game - with changes to building, decorating, and even clothing.

Major Changes

Building upgrades and changes

The buildings available have been changed, with buildings now broken down based on industry instead of raw material. For instance, the new Weaponcrafter building is used to create weapons, shields, and armour - instead of the mason workshop (stone weapons), smithy (metal weapons), carpenter (shields).

Similarly, tools are now all made at the Toolmaker, which is also the source of a great deal of building upgrades.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/efe200bc20dfa8b9e4f5ea3b6f87f0757a8af594.png

Most buildings are now created in a "basic" state, and must be upgraded to reach their full potential. The type of upgrades available depend on the building type, but for instance, crafter buildings can be upgraded to unlock new materials and give quality bonuses to items created there.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/f5db5350c17a340e1a5f1876c16941135d57d701.png

Building Decorations

Buildings can now be decorated using a simplified interface. Some items will even allow you to choose their primary colour, helping you keep to a specific palette. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ee0e55ddf9c3dffa6310dd23080c0502bc104a09.png

Many more items have been added for decorative purposes, including two new classes of decorative items - carpets and wall decorations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4c5e061cfe9142421f5b15290a29a092adfa8b34.png

Clothing

The player character can now change clothing using the new wardrobe item at the house. Clothing however must be unlocked at the tailor workshop. The fancier the clothing, the fancier the material used to create it, including the need for silk - which is not found on your island...

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/4494cb936d6ff57959b751c49d1374569db85ec0.png

Storage

Island storage has been greatly simplified. Instead of having separate chests with their own inventory, now all chests open the same inventory - making it much easier to remember where you left that... thing.

To help with the larger inventory sizes, the interface has been updated to allow for pagination and filtering.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/c635c2a96c105f8bcf2072771633b0305001d1da.png

Trading

Trading has been given a significant boost in importance. Some of the more exotic items can only be accessed via trade. To help one's trading efforts, trading is now performed at the Trade Post - which can be upgraded to increase trader frequency, and even increase the amount of profit the player makes during a trade.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88ca92faeb3ea874dd3ea2f000b1dd4513fa38c3.png

Additionally, trade goods have been introduced. These are items that can be crafted at the appropriate building, and have a higher value compared to others - perfect for squeezing out that extra gold.

And the rest...

There are other changes not mentioned here, so give the game a try and see for yourself. Try out the new decoration features and see what you can come up with.

notes.title: Alone | Domus Update to be released soon
notes.notes:
The Domus Update is a major update for Alone, changing primarily the way you build and decorate your settlement, but also including some other large changes to the peaceful portion of the game.

And it will be released soon - on Sunday 11th June. A summary of the new features and changes are included below, but for more detail you can read the Feature Focuses, or just give it a play and see for yourself.

Because of the major changes, this release is not save game compatible with the previous versions of Alone.

Major Changes

 Buildings can now be upgraded, unlocking more features and bonuses, better quality crafted items, or more items available to be crafted
 Changes to the amount of buildings available - some have been added, removed, or merged
 Building decoration interface simplified and improved
 Added new building decorations, including new types, carpets and wall hangings
 Character can now change clothing, and can unlock new clothing and accessory choices
 Storage is island-wide and accessible through an improved interface


Minor Changes

 Farm plots now belong to farm areas and crops are unlocked through upgrades
 Quest UI is collapsed and is displayed in corner
 Certain items are only available from traders, and certain trade goods have higher cost
 Walls now partially cut away
 New Quests and Achievements

notes.title: Ironwood Update
notes.notes:
The Ironwood Update is now live. With it come major changes to enemies, material unlocking, and includes a couple of interesting boss enemies.

[previewyoutube=TkoV33aTHTc;full][/previewyoutube]

Major Changes

- Changes to the way materials (Iron, Orium, Hardwood &c) are unlocked
- A new type of map - the enchanted forest and enemies to populate it
- Two new boss enemies - and two custom maps to fight them in
- The ship can now be upgraded
- The introduction of cloth, and some other items to farm
- Smarter enemies, ranged enemies, support enemies

This is a major release and save games are unfortunately not compatible. Starting a new game will hide the previous save games.

So, why not give it a try, and share any feedback.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8f5a9d56f8aa141209fc44069df9882811880ba7.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/187bd7fadd0b281c9cb736325cad486110771d8e.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88c66b922679be3575d7a7d0ff4c213d3b179963.png

notes.title: Ironwood Update - Feature Roundup
notes.notes:
I'm pleased to announce that the Ironwood update is feature-done, and only needs some testing and balancing before it's released. No official date just yet, but hopefully in a week or two, depending on how it goes.

So let's take a quick look at what's coming with the next release...

[previewyoutube=TkoV33aTHTc;full][/previewyoutube]

A summary of the changes

- Materials are now unlocked by clearing a mine, or cutting a sapling from the forbidden forests. Also no more multi-ore rocks or multi-wood trees.
- Two boss enemies/arenas to fight in the mine
- A new type of map - the enchanted forest
- Ship upgrades, limited range and cloth
- Smarter enemies, ranged enemies, support enemies

And going into those in a bit more detail...

Material Unlocking
With this next release, you no longer unlock materials (iron, orium, hardwood, heartwood) through capturing specific islands. Since they representing such important milestones, I felt that they deserved having something more interesting.

Let's start with metal. Now you start off with copper rocks on your starting island, and what appears to be an abandoned mine.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/8f5a9d56f8aa141209fc44069df9882811880ba7.png

Unlocking Iron, and Orium require you to defeat specific bosses. The first one is a giant spider which spawns more smaller spiders, whilst the second is an abandoned mining golem which can bring parts of the roof down on your head.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/187bd7fadd0b281c9cb736325cad486110771d8e.png

As you defeat those bosses, the mine becomes usable and you can get all the iron and orium you need from it.

As for wood - now there are special hardwood and heartwood bearing trees, which don't grow on your starting island... initially at least.

But there are enchanted forests available on the world map which have giant world-trees which you can grab a sapling off. If you do so, and survive a return to your ship, these special trees will start growing on your starting island, giving you a supply of these rare woods.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/88c66b922679be3575d7a7d0ff4c213d3b179963.png

Of course, the forests are not unguarded...

Ship upgrades
The ship can now be upgraded. 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/bdd3f2515f7dba0378d416f602729de98921249d.png

This feature brings with it two items of note. Firstly, the first column of upgrades is about extending the ship's range. It's designed in a way that you can't access the more dangerous islands until you unlock iron and hardwood, and the rest until you unlock orium and heartwood - making the progression a bit more clear.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/1d006ae19604019263ad138e5f9edccdf2c985db.png

Also, the speed upgrades require cloth. A new plant has been added which you can farm, then weave into cloth.

Enemies
Enemies are now a bit smarter. Where applicable, they now move in a squad, so fighting them is not as easy as picking them off one at a time. 

Also a bit more variety has been added to enemies. The goblins, dark elves, and everpunished now have their own ranged and support enemy types. The ranged one just makes your life miserable until you get close enough to them to cut them down - having less defense than their peers.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/b4ba825367d21ddec9c8943402e94b77f22ed60c.png

The support unit is different for each of the factions. The Everpunished one for instance, heals their peers - so they might be a priority when fighting them.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/ebf0dc2d179288a9e300df1910ecfceb93fc13f9.jpg

So that's it in terms of major features. There are smaller features which I'll leave as a surprise to discover, and hopefully I'll have an official announcement in a week or two with the actual release.

And for reading this far, you get an image which you can use as a background.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/42309538/494ddea85f0be3ae8884647dfce8ac720d605f56.png
